artifact_assessment.definitional: START outcomes were coded from authorization text: s=authorized always pairs with PERFORMED, and every non-authorized s value pairs with REFUSED (the git event, s=UNK, is the only exception). START is therefore defined over permissions, and its s-witnesses are true by construction.
artifact_assessment.source_genre: The evidence base is a norm register. For norm-making operations (ADOPT, AUTHORIZE, RAISE, ANNOTATE, SUPERSEDE) the row is the act, so these operations are attested. For execution operations (START) and register meta-rules (REGISTER rule, ASSIGN retired, OPEN-WORK by note), the register can only state norms, and the coder turned those norms into counterfactual REFUSED events (ground RULE). Only one execution record (git) was supplied.
artifact_assessment.counter_evidence: The one attested START (the git commit, 08-03 16:10) occurs while the provided sources show WP-4B as unauthorized or blocked (R-72, R-77). If that ordering holds, attested behaviour diverges from the permission-coded outcome. The order of the commit and R-77 within 08-03 is UNKNOWN.
artifact_assessment.consequence: Only a keeps clean strict support on attested acts (2 pairs, both expressing the same Chief-vs-Decision-Authority rule). e keeps weak support (1 cluster pair, half-attested values). c has coarse support only. k, s, t and h have none, and s's apparent support was circular before any filter.
